customer.business: ACHV Performance Systems (Hevadex Malta): 'Protected Handover', peelable OMNIGUARD protection of installed glazing and aluminium/PVC joinery, applied by ACHV-approved applicators with a signed QA handover pack
customer.target: Maltese organisations that carry the cost of damage to installed glazing and joinery before handover: main building contractors, developer-builders and glazing/aluminium installers on multi-unit projects

market_context.text: About 3,000 new dwellings are approved every quarter (3,010 in Q1 and 3,126 in Q2 2026); 72% are apartments, but the average permit covers only about six dwellings, so most jobs are small
Since July 2025 every building contractor must hold a BCA licence; 924 building licences were issued when the law came into force
Most construction firms are very small: about 78% of the 6,028 active construction enterprises are sole traders or partnerships
Maltese businesses take on average about 80 days to pay suppliers, well above the European B2B average of 56 days
Waterproofing and protection materials are cheap and easy to buy locally: roof liquid membranes sell at €3.60–5.00/kg in hardware stores and protection film costs well under €1/m² in material
Prices are quoted ex VAT between businesses; Maltese VAT is 18%

roles.name: Owner or managing director
roles.how: Signs every new supplier and watches cash and margin on each job.

roles.name: Project or site manager
roles.how: Owns the programme and the snagging list; recommends, but does not sign large spends.

roles.name: Quantity surveyor or procurement
roles.how: Compares quotes per m², checks who carries the risk in the subcontract, wants certificates and insurance.

roles.name: Technical director of a glazing contractor

buying_process.name: Owner decides alone
buying_process.how: Decides after one site visit and a quote, usually for the next block.

buying_process.name: Trial on one floor or one block first
buying_process.how: Wants to see it applied and removed on their own site before committing.

buying_process.name: Specified in the subcontract package
buying_process.how: The developer or main contractor decides what protection the subcontractor must provide and who pays.

buying_process.name: Approved supplier list or tender
buying_process.how: A new supplier needs documents, insurance and a credit application before any order.

current_options.name: Self-adhesive film, plastic sheet or board with tape, applied and removed by own labour
current_options.how: Per m² all-in including own labour; ACHV's planning assumption, not a measured local price.

current_options.name: Relies on the factory film already on the aluminium profiles
current_options.how: No extra cost; protects frames for part of the programme but not the glass.

current_options.name: Another peelable or spray-on protective coating
current_options.how: Per m², rarely used locally; price is an assumption.

behaviours.name: Price-led buyer
behaviours.how: Compares cost per m² with film and tape and buys the cheapest that is good enough.

behaviours.name: Relationship buyer
behaviours.how: Buys from suppliers and trades they have worked with for years.

behaviours.name: Programme and quality buyer
behaviours.how: Pays more to avoid snagging delays and callbacks on premium blocks.

behaviours.name: Convenience buyer
behaviours.how: Wants one supplier to take the whole job off their hands.

behaviours.name: Innovator
behaviours.how: Tries new site methods early and likes to show clients something different.

objections.text: Film and tape cost almost nothing; why pay about €19/m²?
We pay our suppliers at 60 to 90 days, not deposits up front
If the coating marks the frame or the coated glass when it comes off, who pays? The manufacturer excludes it
In July and August half the façade is in full sun; when can you even apply it?

objections: ACHV is a contractor too; I don't want a competitor on my site or seeing my programme
The glazing subcontractor is responsible for damage until handover, not me
The aluminium already comes with factory film
I've never seen it used in Malta; show me a local job

pitch:
Protected Handover (ACHV Performance Systems, using HEVADEX OMNIGUARD): a peelable coating sprayed or rolled onto installed glazing and aluminium or PVC frames that protects them from cement, plaster, paint and scratches until handover, then peels off. Applied and removed by an ACHV-approved applicator, with a site survey, a test panel on your frames, supervision on your first job and a signed QA handover pack.
Price: €12.26 per m² to ACHV (product, survey, testing, supervision and QA pack) plus the applicator's labour and preparation, about €6.70 per m², so about €19 per m² ex VAT in total. A 1,000 m² year is about €19,000 all-in.
Minimum 150 m² per job. Removal is scheduled in the quote; the coating must come off within 18 months on windows.
Payment: 50% deposit on the first order, balance before handover; after that, 30 days from invoice after a credit check.
Pilot offer: a paid pilot from 100 m² at the full price, with written pass/fail criteria. If it passes and you order the next building within 90 days, €1 per m² of the pilot is credited against that order.
If you prefer to use your own installer: OMNIGUARD supplied at €15.50 per kg (about €10.20 per m²) with the method statement and substrate exclusion list.
